key_finding: LUNR is a transformation story: FY25 revenue of $250-300M with Q4 at $44.8M and 19% Q4 gross margin gave way to an FY26 outlook of $900M-$1B revenue with positive Adjusted EBITDA — implied 3-4x revenue growth driven by Lanteris acquisition closing (Q1 2026) and NASA CLPS task-order ramp. Total backlog $943M post-Lanteris. NASA CLPS contract ceiling $4.82B with $150M guaranteed near-term. The $800M Lanteris acquisition ($450M cash + $350M stock) is the single most consequential transaction in the company's history.

lanteris_acquisition.strategic_rationale: Transforms Intuitive Machines from pure-play lunar delivery specialist to full space prime contractor
lanteris_acquisition.leadership: Chris Johnson (ex-CEO Lanteris, ex-President Boeing Satellite Systems International) becomes President of Lanteris Space Systems within Intuitive Machines

structural_observations: Q4 2025 revenue down -18% YoY reflects the lumpy NASA milestone-payment recognition pattern — IM-1 mission revenue was recognised in FY24 and FY25 has mostly been preparation for IM-2 and IM-3 deliveries.

FY26 outlook of $900M-$1B revenue requires both Lanteris contribution AND organic lunar-mission contract revenue ramp; the 3-4x growth is more a function of acquisition close than organic operating leverage.
Positive Adjusted EBITDA in FY26 is the operating-profitability inflection — until now Intuitive Machines has been a cash-burning venture-scale operator.
NASA CLPS contract ceiling of $4.82B with $150M guaranteed near-term implies large potential revenue stream contingent on continued task-order awards.
The IM-5 task order ($180.4M) is the largest single CLPS task order awarded to date — uses the larger cargo-class Nova-D lander rather than the Nova-C class used for IM-1 and IM-2.
